title: Alan Grinnell explores shamanism and iconography in ancient Panamanian ceramics
summary: Alan Grinnell, author of Painting the Cosmos: Art and Iconography of the Ceramics of Ancient Panama , discusses what decades of looking at ancient Panamanian pottery have led him to see in an artistic tradition still unfamiliar to many specialists in pre-Columbian art. Drawing on more than 800 vessels, archaeological evidence, early Spanish accounts and his own background as a neuroscientist and biologist, Grinnell considers the possible meanings of hybrid animals, transformed shamans, hidden faces and recurring designs that persisted for centuries. He also addresses the difficulties created by looting and lost archaeological contexts, explains why he believes many of the vessels themselves may have been regarded as living beings, and reflects on the questions that future excavations and scientific analysis might finally answer. title: Sotheby's to auction landmark scientific first editions and Newton manuscript from private collection
summary: This October, Sotheby's will present the first installment of Reason and Revolution: Extraordinary Works from a Distinguished Private Collection, a dedicated single-owner auction devoted to the history of scientific thought. Headlined by first editions from Nicolaus Copernicus, Galileo Galilei, Johannes Kepler, and Isaac Newton, alongside a rare surviving manuscript in Newton's own hand, the sale reunites landmark works that, in several cases, have not appeared on the market in more than three decades. A number of these highlights passed through the same distinguished library of Sturgis S. Dunham, and his son, Robert S. Dunham, before entering the present collection, underscoring the depth and continuity of scholarship behind the group as a whole. title: The Perimeter presents Magali Reus' first institutional London exhibition since 2018
summary: The Perimeter opened Swimming by Night, Magali Reus’ first institutional exhibition in London since 2018. Four bodies of new and recent works – Merlin (2024), Streamers (2025), Rig (2025–26) and Subs (2026) – are brought into dialogue with site-specific wall renderings and architectural interventions. Rooted by an interest in ecology and systems of production, this exhibition speaks to the relationship between nature, technology and the impact of post-industrial human activity. Together, these works play with the dynamics of attention, where objects become carriers of competing narratives around desire, consumption and transformation. Constructed using varied techniques of fabrication, ranging from the handcrafted to the industrial, Reus’ process unfolds through its own material language, where forms and symbols feel familiar yet not immediately determinable. title: Vatican Apostolic Library explores water, catastrophe, and wonder in major new initiative
summary: His Holiness Pope Leo XIV inaugurated AQVA, the landmark exhibition of the Vatican Apostolic Library’s new five-year cycle, Catastrophe and Wonder (Catastrofe e Meraviglia). Marking a dynamic new chapter in the Library's centuries-long mission of preservation and public engagement, the ambitious multi-year initiative offers a wide-ranging, interdisciplinary exploration of the natural elements — framing them as mirrors to humanity’s deepest fears and highest hopes. Conceived as an immersive journey through the environmental and human threats that have historically imperilled the written word — ranging from water and fire to light, insects, and human intervention — Catastrophe and Wonder invites visitors to look beyond fear to discover new avenues of interpretation and artistic creation. title: Guggenheim appoints Maria Kanakis Yang Deputy Director
summary: The Guggenheim New York announces the appointment of Maria Kanakis Yang as Deputy Director of the museum. Yang will report directly to Melissa Chiu, Director of the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum and will work closely with her along with colleagues across the museum to advance key institutional priorities, strengthen cross-departmental processes, operations, visitor experience, and strategic initiatives. Yang brings more than 15 years of executive leadership experience in cultural institutions, with expertise spanning organizational strategy, institutional advancement, governance, and cross-functional collaboration. In this role, Yang will focus on ensuring the structures, resources, and collaboration needed to support the museum’s mission are as strong as possible. Her appointment comes as the Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation prepares to undertake a strategic planning process.

title: Graziella Patiño de Ortiz Linares Collection sale achieves €38.7 million in Paris
summary: At Christie's, the Graziella Patiño de Ortiz Linares Collection achieved a resounding success, realising €38,736,120. Heralded as a landmark sale, it more than fulfilled expectations, surpassing its high estimate by a substantial margin, with 64% of lots selling above their high estimates. Christie's saleroom was filled to capacity for this highly anticipated auction, eagerly awaited by collectors and connoisseurs of the Grand Goût and eighteenth-century French art. The results reflect the remarkable coherence of the collection, with each work embodying Graziella's relentless pursuit of excellence and uncompromising standards. Comprising 59 exceptional lots, the sale was led by an outstanding group of paintings dedicated to the greatest names in French art and some of their most celebrated masterpieces. title: Boturini Codex travels to Paris in reciprocal Mexico-France cultural exchange
summary: One of the most important surviving visual records of Mexica migration has arrived in Paris, where the Boturini Codex is now on view at the museum of the Bibliothèque nationale de France through December 13, 2026. The display places the early 16th-century Indigenous manuscript in an unexpected architectural setting: the Galerie Mazarin, where figures from Greco-Roman mythology look down on images of Huitzilopochtli and the migration of the Mexica people. The encounter brings together two very different visual traditions while marking 200 years of diplomatic relations between Mexico and France. The exhibition is part of a reciprocal cultural exchange organized by Mexico’s Ministry of Culture, through the National Institute of Anthropology and History, and France’s Ministry of Culture, through the BnF. title: Christie's Hong Kong to offer major Chinese paintings from distinguished private collections
summary: Christie’s will bring together centuries of Chinese painting and calligraphy this October in Hong Kong, with two sales drawing on works from prominent private collections in Asia, Europe and the United States. The auctions, scheduled for October 27 and 28 during Hong Kong Asian Art Week, range from Yuan and Ming dynasty masters to some of the defining figures of 20th-century Chinese ink painting. The first sale, Fine Chinese Classical Paintings and Calligraphy, takes place on October 27 and is led by Bada Shanren’s Flowers and Birds, a 1699 album of twelve leaves estimated at HK$12 million to HK$18 million. title: Marcel Duchamp Prize winner Xie Lei explores emotion and figure in 'Pain of Others'
summary: François Ghebaly presents Pain of Others, an exhibition of new paintings by Xie Lei. The exhibition marks the artist’s debut solo presentation with the gallery and his first in Los Angeles, opening in Beverly Hills at 415 N Camden Dr. Pain of Others continues French-Chinese artist Xie Lei’s investigation into the possibilities of representing our most elemental emotional states. The artist’s paintings develop from meticulously-applied layers of oil paint that give his surfaces a breathlike shimmer, in a palette of phosphorescent blues, Sèvres greens, or warm ochres that provide a blanketed, nocturnal quality to his scenes. The indeterminate spaces of his paintings are lit almost entirely by figures which possess a luminosity that radiates from the deepest underlayers of their forms. title: Bechtler Museum spotlights four generations of Latin American printmakers
summary: Bechtler Museum of Modern Art presents Making an Impression: Pioneering Latin American Printmakers, a major exhibition that brings together works by Rufino Tamayo (Mexican, 1899–1991), Jesús Rafael Soto (Venezuelan, 1923–2005), Regina Silveira (Brazilian, born 1939) and Analia Saban (Argentinian, born 1980). On view from September 26, 2026, through February 1, 2027, and curated by Bechtler Curator Dr. Katia Zavistovski, the exhibition examines how artists across generations have transformed the possibilities of printmaking through material and perceptual innovation. Spanning works on paper, sculptural editions, vinyl installations, and technologically driven processes, Making an Impression highlights printmaking as a dynamic field of experimentation that continually redefines the relationship between image, surface and space. title: Ai Weiwei unveils major public artwork 'Mushrooms' at MCA Australia
summary: The Museum of Contemporary Art Australia, alongside the Balnaves Foundation in honour of Neil Balnaves AO, today unveiled Mushrooms, a major new temporary public artwork by internationally acclaimed artist Ai Weiwei for the Neil Balnaves Tallawoladah Lawn Commission series. Installed in front of MCA Australia on Tallawoladah Lawn, overlooking Warrane/Sydney Harbour, Mushrooms invites audiences to meditate on the fragility of life during times of conflict and division. title: Ar/Ge Kunst explores states of waiting, land occupation, and genocide in three solo exhibitions
summary: Ar/Ge Kunst’s fall–winter 2026–27 exhibition program unfolds through three exhibitions by Nataliya Zuban, Reem Masri, and Yadykar Ibraimov. Taken together, the three exhibitions are vigilant toward the present, approaching it not as a stable point in time, but as a condition of unseparated experience. That these geographies of genocide, invasion, and incarceration belong to each other, are each other’s missing dark water, and that each of them are ours, is the question and the research of this cycle of exhibitions. Condition of Suspended Present is an exhibition in which ceramics, machines, and sound give material form to states of waiting. title: Christie's brings anime icons from Pikachu to Totoro and Akira back to auction in New York
summary: Pikachu, Goku, Totoro and Kaneda are returning to Christie’s this fall as the auction house continues its exploration of Japanese popular culture with Anime Starts Here: Japanese Subculture Reimagines Tradition, an online sale running from October 9 through 22, 2026. The auction follows Christie’s first edition of Anime Starts Here in March, when a mix of anime, manga and contemporary art influenced by those traditions brought $1,442,466—four times the sale’s low estimate. For the October edition, Christie’s is narrowing the focus more directly onto anime and manga themselves, offering original production material connected with some of the most recognizable characters and films to emerge from Japan over the past several decades. title: Heritage Auctions to feature 70 rare early English Bibles from the Estate of Robert Funk
summary: The history of the Bible in English is also a history of contested authority: who could translate Scripture, who could print it, who could read it and which version church and crown would sanction. More than 70 early Bibles and devotional works from the Estate of Robert Funk, Oklahoma, will bring that history into unusually concentrated view in Heritage’s Oct. 14 Rare Books Signature® Auction. Extending from the English Reformation through the Restoration, the Funk Collection encompasses the principal textual traditions that shaped the English Bible, among them the translations associated with William Tyndale, Miles Coverdale, John Rogers’ “Matthew’s Bible,” the Great Bible, the Geneva Bible and the King James, or Authorized, Version. title: A bottle of the world's most valuable whisky to lead Sotheby's landmark sale at The Macallan Estate
summary: This autumn, Sotheby's and The Macallan will present the first auction ever to take place at The Macallan Estate in Speyside, Scotland – Live from The Macallan Estate. Scheduled for 9 October 2026 and expected to attract the world’s most dedicated whisky collectors, the sale will comprise whiskies from The Macallan drawn almost exclusively from private collections. Conceived to mark the centenary of the distillation of The Macallan 1926, the auction will bring together a selection of the brand’s finest and most sought-after single malts, spanning decades. title: Kunsthalle Zürich presents Ayo Akingbade's first institutional solo exhibition outside the UK
summary: With Crossing, Kunsthalle Zürich presents the first institutional solo exhibition outside the United Kingdom by London-based filmmaker and artist Ayo Akingbade (b. 1994, London). Bringing together two new productions which have their premiere at Kunsthalle Zürich, as well as earlier works by the artist, the exhibition traces Akingbade’s continued engagement with urbanism and architecture and the social and political forces that shape them. Over the past decade, Akingbade has realised over twenty short films that move between the genres of experimental documentary, fiction, and personal essay film, presenting them in both art exhibitions and cinema settings. title: "Constellations" inaugurates the Fondation Beyeler's newly expanded ensemble
summary: “Constellations” inaugurates the Fondation Beyeler’s newly expanded ensemble, unfolding across both museum buildings and throughout the enlarged expanse of the park. Individual works will further be featured in the repurposed historical buildings. The exhibition brings together over 200 outstanding works from the museum’s own collection and from private collections closely connected to the institution, giving rise to unique constellations of art, architecture and nature. “Constellations” unfolds across the Fondation Beyeler’s two museum buildings—Renzo Piano’s iconic Beyeler Museum and Peter Zumthor’s new Wyss Museum. The two buildings offer different perspectives onto the artworks on display. title: Josh Benesh appointed Global Head of Pop Culture for Christie's
summary: Christie's announced the appointment of Josh Benesh as Global Head of Christie's Pop Culture at Christie's, based in New York. Benesh will lead an international team of specialists and work closely with clients and collectors across categories to drive the auction house's growth and expansion across new and emerging markets in the Christie's Pop Culture vertical. The Christie's pop culture team will hold multiple annual auctions celebrating the iconic objects, personas, and achievements that define our collective culture. title: Musée Carnavalet opens 'Nouveau Paris' featuring major donations from Christo and JR
summary: As the Musée Carnavalet - Histoire de Paris has just celebrated its 160th anniversary, the Parisian institution is presenting a new exhibition in the final room of its collection tour, dedicated to Paris from 1977 to the present day. Titled Nouveau Paris, it offers renewed perspectives on the capital’s recent history and explores the transformations that have shaped the lives of Parisians. Featuring nearly thirty works from the museum’s collections, the exhibition—opening Friday, September 25—invites visitors to admire two exceptional donations: one from the Christo and Jeanne-Claude Foundation and the other from JR. These artists have in common their lasting legacy on the contemporary history of the City of Light through their temporary installations. title: The FLAG Art Foundation presents 'Clockwork', a solo exhibition by Sable Elyse Smith
summary: The FLAG Art Foundation is presenting Clockwork, a solo exhibition featuring new and recent work by Sable Elyse Smith, the 2026 recipient of the Suzanne Deal Booth / FLAG Art Foundation Prize, on view September 24, 2026–February 13, 2027. Following its presentation at The Contemporary Austin, FLAG reframes Clockwork by expanding its more cinematic elements into an immersive stage set environment, where video becomes an immediate means of visualizing unseen, ordinary violence. Including sculpture, video, neon, and photography, Clockwork interrogates the fundamental systems of power that define contemporary society, as well as their cultural and psychological impacts. title: Sapar Contemporary presents first solo exhibition by Kalmyk-American artist Sasha Stiles
summary: Sapar Contemporary is presenting a solo exhibition by Sasha Stiles, a first-generation Kalmyk-American artist and poet. This is the gallery’s first exhibition of works by Stiles, who embarks on a deeply personal exploration of poetry as a technology of inheritance. Drawing on Jangar — a centuries-old Kalmyk-Mongolian epic that has survived migration, persecution, deportation, and diaspora — Stiles returns to a foundational story of her nomadic heritage to consider how language, memory, and culture are carried forward, or fall silent. Working across voice, script, print, code, and generative systems, Stiles continues Jangar's living tradition, using ancient practices of oral transmission, portable memory, and embodied knowledge to offer new ways of understanding our increasingly networked, mobile, and computational world. title: Art Museum RIGA BOURSE presents 'Cornucopia', exploring institutional abundance and rare collection works
summary: Cornucopia, an exhibition from the museum’s collection, is on view at the Art Museum RIGA BOURSE in Riga (Doma laukums 6) from 26 September 2026 to 3 January 2027. The cornucopia, usually depicted in a positive and affirmative form, symbolises unlimited material and spiritual abundance. In a sense, a museum with its collection is also like a cornucopia: only a small part of its riches is visible, while the rest waits in storage for researchers and exhibition curators. And yet… What is a museum today? What kinds of exhibitions are created, and for whom? Can anything become an exhibit, and does the “cornucopia” also have limits to its capacity? title: Christie's Paris to stage major October sales led by Monet, Mitchell, Modigliani and historic collections
summary: Christie’s is preparing an ambitious week of Modern and Contemporary art sales in Paris this October, bringing together major private collections, fresh-to-market works and a broad sweep of art from Impressionism to the post-war period. The Paris programme, running from October 16 to 23 during Art Basel Paris, forms part of Christie’s wider autumn 20th- and 21st-century season, which begins in London with its traditional 20/21 Marquee Week from October 14 to 16. In Paris, the auction house will stage four sales centered on important international collections and works that have remained outside the market for years. Among the collections taking center stage are those connected with the Durand-Ruel family, Antonio Homem Sonnabend, Marlene and Spencer Hays, and the group known as Radiant Modernism. title: Bob Dylan's handwritten lyrics for two 'Blood on the Tracks' songs sell for $290,404 at auction
summary: Bob Dylan’s handwritten working lyrics for two songs from Blood on the Tracks, “Idiot Wind” and “You’re Gonna Make Me Lonesome When You Go,” sold for $290,404 in RR Auction’s Remarkable Rarities sale, which concluded Sept. 24. The double-sided sheet contains working lyrics for “Idiot Wind” on one side and a nearly complete working draft of “You’re Gonna Make Me Lonesome When You Go” on the reverse. Dylan wrote the latter under its working title, “You’re Gonna Make Me Miss You When You Go.” The manuscript includes revisions, discarded passages and an additional verse absent from the released recording. The archive also includes a two-sided handwritten transcription of “You’re Gonna Make Me Lonesome When You Go” by Ellen Ziffren, who was known to Dylan in 1974 as Ellen Bernstein.
